premises.text: RedBeacon lets consumers request local services and book from providers who quote price and appointment times online for transparency and convenience
premises.evidence_span: it's a website where you can request virtually any kind of local service

premises.text: Providers pay only when a consumer books and work is done—full pay-for-performance—easing marketplace chicken-and-egg signup
premises.evidence_span: we're only going to charge businesses if a consumer books the job with them and actually does work

premises.text: Consumers need rich trust info before booking—friends/family recommendations, references, web ratings/reviews, background checks—so the product must be social
premises.evidence_span: consumers actually needed a lot more information than we thought they would before they'll book a job online

premises.text: Geographic expansion from Bay Area learning market into Seattle and more cities with high-quality providers
premises.evidence_span: officially, Red Beacon is open in Seattle now

premises.text: Embeddable customized widget exposes the provider network on partner sites with occupation filters, branding, recommendations, dashboard, and generous revenue share
premises.evidence_span: we're creating an embeddable widget which basically makes our high-quality service provider network available to any website

value.text: Easy online booking of local services with price transparency like booking a flight
value.evidence_span: increase the price transparency and make it very easy to schedule jobs online, which is just incredibly convenient

causal_links.evidence_span: local businesses who've signed up for Red Beacon receive the job, and they're able to quote a price and offer appointment times
Red Beacon is open in Seattle now. And there'll be many other markets coming soon
These are now available to your users if you own a website with one line of JavaScript

notes: Core marketplace + pay-for-performance + social trust info kept as one revisable marketplace theory (lessons learned as continuing conditions). Bootstrap/fundraising narrative excluded (§4.2). Seattle expansion and embed widget split as separately announced go-to-market modules. Named media partners treated as traction of widget GTM, not extra premises. Live demo customization folded into widget premise (§4.1.7).
